title: CPU Architecture, Registers and Fetch–Execute Cycle
intro: A short, self-paced catch-up covering the essential lesson ideas. Check every question, then correct anything missed.

stages.label: Remember
stages.lead: Recall two useful ideas from earlier lessons.

questions.prompt: Which technology is found in a USB flash drive?
questions.feedback: Flash drives use solid-state memory without moving read/write heads.

questions.prompt: Why might compressing a file make it faster to transfer?
questions.feedback: A smaller file generally involves fewer bits being transmitted.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the essential ideas and worked example before checking your understanding.

blocks.title: CPU roles
blocks.text: The Control Unit coordinates operations and decodes instructions; the ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.

blocks.title: Registers
blocks.text: PC: next instruction address; MAR: address being accessed; MDR: transferred data/instruction; ACC: calculation result.

blocks.title: Kitchen memory aid
blocks.text: PC = recipe bookmark; MAR = shelf location; MDR = ingredient fetched; ACC = mixing bowl for results.

blocks.title: Instruction cycle
blocks.text: Fetch the instruction, decode it and execute it; then repeat. Cache keeps frequently used data and instructions close to the CPU.

blocks.title: Visual model · CPU Architecture, Registers and Fetch–Execute Cycle
blocks.caption: During a fetch the PC supplies the next address; MAR receives the access address and MDR receives the transferred instruction.

blocks.title: Worked model · Explain a fetch using the PC, MAR, MDR and the Control Unit.
blocks.text: The PC identifies the address of the next instruction. The address is copied to MAR. The requested instruction transfers from memory into MDR. The PC updates to reference the next instruction in sequence. The Control Unit decodes the fetched instruction; it can then be executed, possibly using the ALU.

items: MAR — Stores the address of a memory location being accessed.
PC — Stores address of the next instruction.

questions.prompt: Which CPU component performs arithmetic and logic?
questions.feedback: The Arithmetic Logic Unit performs these operations.

questions.prompt: Which register normally stores the address of the next instruction?
questions.feedback: The Program Counter identifies where to fetch the next instruction.

options: Data or an instruction being transferred
questions.answer: Data or an instruction being transferred
questions.feedback: The Memory Data Register holds data/instructions transferred to or from memory.

stages.label: Practise
stages.lead: Match, reorder and apply what you have learnt.

blocks.text: The address and the data being transferred are held in different registers.

questions.prompt: Match the register to its main job.
questions.feedback: PC, MAR and MDR have distinct roles in fetching.

questions.prompt: Put the three phases of the CPU instruction cycle in order.
Which register is often used to hold an ALU calculation result?
questions.feedback: The accumulator may hold the result of an ALU calculation.

questions.prompt: What does the Control Unit primarily do?
questions.feedback: The Control Unit coordinates CPU actions and decodes instructions.

questions.prompt: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.
questions.feedback: The Arithmetic Logic Unit is responsible for such operations.

questions.prompt: The MDR is the register that identifies the next instruction address.
questions.feedback: The PC has that role; MDR holds transferred data/instructions.

questions.prompt: Fetch, decode and execute are stages of CPU instruction processing.
questions.feedback: The CPU repeatedly carries out the instruction cycle.
